rules.statement: Never combine whey/dairy protein powder with high-vitamin-C citrus (lemon, amla, orange, mosambi) in the same drink — the acid curdles the milk protein into a lumpy texture. Use a non-citrus fruit (banana, mango, papaya) instead.
rules.rationale: Citric/ascorbic acid drops dairy protein below its isoelectric point, denaturing and clumping it — a real curdling reaction, not a taste preference.

rules.statement: Protein powder (whey or plant) must never appear in a snack or salad option — protein there comes from whole food only (paneer, egg, chicken, sprouts, peanuts, chana).

During Menstrual phase, don't build an option primarily around heavy dairy (paneer/curd as the dominant ingredient) when the point is iron replenishment — calcium inhibits non-heme iron absorption. Pair iron sources (dates, beetroot, moong, sesame) with vitamin C instead of a large dairy portion.
rules.rationale: Calcium and phytates in dairy bind non-heme iron in the gut, meaningfully reducing absorption.

rules.statement: When a dish includes turmeric/haldi, prefer also including a pinch of black pepper (kali mirch) — piperine significantly boosts curcumin absorption.
rules.rationale: Piperine inhibits the liver's rapid metabolism of curcumin, increasing its bioavailability manyfold.

rules.statement: Raw sprouted/fermented dishes suit Follicular/Ovulatory digestion; avoid raw sprouts as the primary ingredient in a Menstrual or Luteal option.
rules.rationale: Raw legume sprouts are harder to digest; Menstrual/Luteal favor cooked, warming preparation.

rules.statement: When peanuts/peanut butter are a primary ingredient (not a garnish), make that clear in `why` or `description`, not buried only in `key_ingredients`, so a peanut-allergic user can spot and skip it.

The user has an insulin-resistance/PCOS/diabetes-like flag — don't make a high-glycemic fruit (banana, mango, dates in quantity) the dominant carb in the fruit-category option. Pair with protein/fiber or use a lower-GI fruit (berries, guava, apple).
rules.rationale: High-GI carbs eaten alone spike insulin more sharply, which is specifically counter-productive for insulin-resistant/PCOS profiles.

rules.statement: Menstrual and Luteal phase options must be served warm or room temperature, never cold.
rules._enforcement: Already enforced via the serving_style field + servingViolation check in evaluateChefOptionsQuality — this entry is documentation only, no detection block here.
